nodes.name: IF Cleaning
nodes.procedure: To remove the oxide of IF, the commercial IF was washed with 1 M HCl and copiously cleaned with deionized water.
nodes.source_text: To remove the oxide of IF, the commercial IF was washed with 1 M HCl and copiously cleaned with deionized water.

nodes.name: Ni/Fe3O4/IF Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Meanwhile, 2 mmol Ni(NO3)2 powder was dissolved in 40 mL deionized water with the application of magnetic stirring. Subsequently, 10 mL H2O2 was dropped into the above solution. The as-obtained solution and the cleaned IF substrate were then transferred into a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave, where a hydrothermal reaction was conducted at 80 °C for 24 h. The obtained product was washed several times with deionized water and ethanol. It was then dried in a vacuum at 60 °C overnight. The final product was the Ni/Fe3O4/IF catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Ni/Fe3O4/IF show diffraction peaks at 35°, 57°, 62° for Fe3O4 (311), (511), (440) planes and 51° for Ni (200) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction peaks located at 35°, 57°, and 62° in the XRD patterns of the Fe3O4/IF and Ni/Fe3O4/IF catalysts (Fig. 2a) are attributed to (311), (511), and (440) planes of Fe3O4 (PDF#89-3854), respectively. A characteristic peak at about 51° in the XRD patterns of the Ni/Fe3O4/IF catalyst is accurately indexed to the (200) plane of cubic Ni (PDF#65-2865).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Ni/Fe3O4/IF and Fe3O4/IF catalysts with needle arrays uniformly grown on IF substrate, heights ~1 μm and ~0.5 μm respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-obtained Fe3O4 and Ni/Fe3O4 catalysts appear to be uniformly grown on the IF substrate. They exhibit similar needle arrays and the heights of these needles are about 0.5 and 1 μm for the Fe3O4/IF (Fig. 2b) and Ni/Fe3O4/IF (Fig. 2c) catalysts, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of Ni/Fe3O4 shows lattice fringes of 0.47 nm for Fe3O4 (111) plane and 0.20 nm for Ni (111) plane with well-matched heterointerface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice fringe space of 0.47 nm (Fig. 2e) corresponds to the (111) plane of Fe3O4, while the typical interfering distance of 0.20 nm is associated with the lattice spacing of the (111) plane of the Ni phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Fe, Ni, O in Ni/Fe3O4/IF; Ni 2p shows Ni⁰ at 852.5 eV, Ni²⁺ at 855.2 eV, Ni³⁺ at 856.5 eV; Fe 2p peaks at 711.3, 719.5, 724.3, 733.4 eV corresponding to Fe 2p3/2, sat, 2p1/2, sat; O 1s Ni/Fe-O at 530.1 eV with binding energy shift evidencing Ni-Fe3O4 interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Their XPS survey spectra illustrate the presence of Fe, Ni, and O in the Ni/Fe3O4/IF catalyst... In Ni 2p XPS spectra of the Fe3O4/IF and Ni/Fe3O4/IF catalysts (Fig. 3a), the Ni species... Ni⁰ (852.5 eV), Ni²⁺ (855.2 eV), Ni³⁺ (856.5 eV)... In the XPS Fe 2p spectra... 711.3, 719.5, 724.3, and 733.4 eV, corresponding to Fe 2p3/2, Fe 2p3/2 sat, Fe 2p1/2, and Fe 2p1/2 sat... In O 1s spectra... the peak at about 530.1 eV is attributed to Ni/Fe-O... the shift in binding energy of Fe-O peak provides the evidence of an interaction.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES of Ni/Fe3O4 shows decreased white line intensity vs Fe3O4 indicating electron transfer from Ni to Fe3O4; FT-EXAFS peaks at 1.3 Å (Fe-O) and 2.5 Å (Fe-Fe/Ni) with longer Fe-Fe/Ni bond and WT maximum at 4.1 Å⁻¹ (vs 3.5 Å⁻¹ for Fe3O4) confirming electron redistribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure spectroscopy (XANES) spectrum of the Ni/Fe3O4 catalyst (Fig. 3d) shows the decreased white line intensity relative to a Fe3O4 catalyst... The peaks in the extended XAFS (EXAFS) curves... at about 1.3 and 2.5 Å are attributed to Fe-O and Fe-Fe/Ni bond... Among the wavelet transforms (WT) for the k²-weighted Fe K-edge EXAFS curves... the Ni/Fe3O4 catalyst reveals the intensity maximum at 4.1 Å⁻¹, associated with the Fe-O bond, which exhibits a positive shift in contrast to that of Fe3O4 (3.5 Å⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV gives Cdl values of 4.5 mF cm⁻² for Ni/Fe3O4/IF, 3.2 mF cm⁻² for Fe3O4/IF, and 2.2 mF cm⁻² for IrO2/IF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In this case, the calculated Cdl values of the Ni/Fe3O4/IF, Fe3O4/IF, and IrO2/IF catalysts (Fig. 4d) are 4.5, 3.2, and 2.2 mF cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows Ni/Fe3O4/IF has smaller charge-transfer resistance Rct than Fe3O4/IF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical impedance spectra of these used catalysts (Fig. 4e and Fig. S6) show that the Ni/Fe3O4/IF catalyst owns the smaller charge-transfer resistance (Rct) than the Fe3O4/IF catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-vis absorption spectra (Tauc plot) show narrowed bandgap for Ni/Fe3O4/IF vs Fe3O4/IF due to delocalized electrons; valence band spectra show stronger peak intensity for Ni/Fe3O4/IF indicating more d-electrons.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The valence bands and bandgaps (obtained from UV-vis absorption spectra by Tauc plot) of the Fe3O4/IF and Ni/Fe3O4/IF catalysts were calculated. The peak intensity of the Ni/Fe3O4/IF catalyst is stronger than that of the Fe3O4/IF catalyst (Fig. 3c)... The narrowed bandgap of the Ni/Fe3O4/IF catalyst affords efficient electron exchange (Fig. S3d).
